\begin{document}
We use the reduced energy
\begin{equation}
x \equiv \beta\epsilon .
\label{eq:x}
\end{equation}
At high temperature, $x \to 0$, the occupation is
\begin{equation}
\frac{1}{e^{x}+1} = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{x}{4} + O(x^3) .
\label{eq:ht}
\end{equation}
\end{document}
